answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token bond before it may submit work, with the bond increasing for high-impact actions. Independent reviewers challenge a random sample of outputs; when a fraud claim is upheld, the bond is slashed and paid partly to the challenger. This makes a sybil swarm costly: each fake identity needs capital, and repeated deception risks losing it. The onyx orchard can track bonds, while a vertex in the review graph identifies which claims need scrutiny.
